topics.label: Introduction to the lecture
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic provides the opening framing by introducing complement, its complexity, and its significance in immunology.

topics.label: Foundations and central role of C3 in complement
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics establish the foundational concepts, nomenclature conventions, and the central role of C3 activation in the complement cascade.

topics.label: Pathways of complement activation
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics describe the three recognition pathways that initiate complement and converge to reach the trigger threshold of C3 activation.

topics.label: Effector mechanisms of complement
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics detail the downstream effector processes through which activated complement targets and destroys pathogens.

topics.label: Regulation of complement on host cells
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic explains the regulatory proteins and mechanisms that protect host tissues from accidental complement-mediated destruction.

topics.label: Clinical consequences of complement deficiencies
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic outlines the distinct clinical presentations and disease phenotypes that arise from deficiencies in specific complement components.

topics.label: Pathogen evasion of complement
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic examines the molecular strategies evolved by pathogens to resist and evade complement-mediated killing.

topics.label: Lecture conclusion
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic provides the closing framing by concluding the complement topic and previewing the next lecture in the series.
